name: Assess mental health crises in the emergency department
summary: When a person comes to the emergency department in a mental health crisis, the emergency physician first rules out a medical cause and then asks the hospital's crisis team for an assessment. A crisis clinician interviews the patient and family, assesses suicide and violence risk, and either arranges discharge with a safety plan and follow-up or asks the on-call psychiatrist to decide on admission, which may be involuntary under the Mental Health Act. Patients at risk are searched, held on a Form 1 and watched constantly, often for many hours, because crisis clinicians are not on site overnight, psychiatrists are on call, and psychiatric beds are scarce.

baseline.org_archetype: A three-site Ontario community hospital corporation with about 130,000 to 160,000 ED visits a year, an extended-hours emergency mental health crisis team and a 40-bed inpatient psychiatry unit.
baseline.notes: Unit of work is one crisis assessment requested by an emergency physician. Triage, medical assessment and the boarding of admitted patients are separate processes (ed-patient-triage, ed-physician-assessment, ed-admission-boarding).

unit_of_work: one ED mental health crisis assessment
trigger: After medical assessment the emergency physician requests a mental health crisis consult in the hospital information system and by phone.
end_state: The patient is discharged with a safety plan and a referral, an admission order is written for the inpatient psychiatry unit, or a transfer to another hospital's psychiatric bed is requested.

volume.seasonality: Fairly even across the year with more evening and weekend presentations; youth presentations rose during the 2020-2022 pandemic waves.

evidence.note: Author's estimate: about 3% to 4% of the corporation's 10,500 to 13,500 monthly ED visits get a crisis-team assessment. At an academic downtown hospital 8.1% of ED visits were mental health visits (baia2019); a suburban community hospital has a lower share and not every mental health visit needs the crisis team.

surge.cause: COVID-19 pandemic waves shifting mental health presentations to the ED while community services were closed or virtual

evidence.note: Author's estimate for 2020-2022; no corporation-level data found.

About 2.3 hours per assessment for 450 assessments a month is about 8 FTE; the rest of the crisis team's 25 headcount covers part-time positions, follow-up clinics and evening coverage at three sites.
Consult request, Form 1 and discharge decisions take about 15 to 20 minutes per case.
Risk screen, observation checks and discharge for each patient.
Handles elopements and police notification.
Searches, police hand-over and constant observation of patients held on a Form 1; in many Ontario EDs security officers or sitters do this observation.
On-call psychiatrists assess about half of crisis patients, during the day on site and after hours by coming in or the next morning.
Arranges transfers when no psychiatric bed is available in the corporation.

systems.name: Hospital information system (electronic patient record with ADT, order entry, results, eMAR and clinical documentation)
Ontario Laboratories Information System and ConnectingOntario viewer
Electronic bed board and patient flow dashboard
Email, telephone, pagers and wireless phones
Fax (referrals, requisitions and reports to community physicians)
Safety incident and complaints reporting system
Document imaging and scanning of paper chart forms

resources.name: Emergency treatment spaces, large site (stretchers, chairs and resuscitation bays)

steps.name: Request crisis consult and decide on holding
steps.description: The emergency physician finishes the medical assessment (vital signs, blood alcohol or drug screen when indicated, physical causes ruled out), documents medical clearance and orders the crisis consult. The physician decides whether the patient's risk means they must be held if they try to leave.

error.defect_description: Medical cause (delirium, intoxication, overdose) not fully excluded before the consult.

next.condition: patient at risk and may leave: hold on Form 1

evidence.note: Share held on Form 1 (about a third of crisis consults) is the author's estimate for Ontario community EDs.

steps.name: Complete Form 1 and give Form 42
steps.description: The physician fills in Form 1 (Application by Physician for Psychiatric Assessment), choosing the Box A serious-harm grounds or Box B, records the facts observed and reported, signs it, and gives the patient Form 42, the notice of the reasons and of the right to a lawyer.

error.defect_description: Form 1 incomplete or grounds not stated, making the detention legally defective.

control.basis: Mental Health Act (Ontario) s.15 and Form 1: physician examination within 7 days; detention for psychiatric assessment up to 72 hours

evidence.note: Form 1 content, the seven-day examination rule and the 72-hour maximum (form1); Form 42 given immediately in a Schedule 1 facility (psychdb_f1).

steps.name: Search the patient and move to a safe room
steps.description: Two security officers explain the search, check the patient and belongings for weapons, medications and ligature risks, store the belongings, have the patient change into a hospital gown and move them to a safe room or a stretcher in view of the nursing station.

control.basis: ED mental health safety policy: search for weapons and ligature risks, safe room

next.condition: came on their own or with family

evidence.note: Search practice from general knowledge of Ontario ED mental health safety policies; share brought by police (about a quarter) estimated.

steps.name: Take custody of the patient from police
steps.description: For a patient brought in by police under the Mental Health Act, security and the nurse complete the joint risk form with the officers, take their report and documentation, and release them once hospital security can safely watch the patient. Much of the police wait happens earlier, during triage and medical assessment.

control.basis: Police-hospital transition protocol (joint risk assessment before officers leave)

evidence.note: Joint risk-assessment hand-over protocol and average police waits of 80 to 125 minutes at one Ontario hospital (hd_police); only the part after the consult request is counted here.

steps.name: Screen suicide risk and set the observation level
steps.description: The emergency nurse completes the suicide risk screening tool, checks the safe room, and sets the observation level with the physician: constant one-to-one observation for high-risk or Form 1 patients, or checks every 15 minutes for others.

error.defect_description: Risk underestimated; observation level too low.

control.basis: Accreditation Canada required organizational practice: suicide risk assessment

evidence.note: Suicide risk screening is an Accreditation Canada required organizational practice; observation shares estimated.

steps.name: Watch the patient constantly until the crisis clinician comes
steps.description: A security officer stays within sight of the patient, logs behaviour on the observation sheet every 15 minutes, and calls the nurse if the patient becomes agitated or tries to leave. Overnight the patient waits until the crisis team starts in the morning.

evidence.note: Elapsed observation time equals the wait for a crisis clinician (author's estimate of 15 minutes to 9 hours; the team works extended hours, not overnight). The officer is paid for the whole watch, so it is recorded as hands-on time.

steps.name: Check the patient every 15 minutes while waiting
steps.description: The nurse or assistant checks the voluntary patient every 15 minutes, offers food and fluids, and reassesses if the patient's mood or behaviour changes, while the patient waits on a stretcher or in the waiting area for the crisis clinician.

evidence.note: Wait for a crisis clinician from 15 minutes to about 9 hours overnight; author's estimate.

steps.name: Review the chart and prior history
steps.description: The crisis clinician reads the ED notes and labs, looks up previous visits, psychiatric admissions and outpatient notes in the hospital information system and the ConnectingOntario viewer, and checks whether the patient has a community case manager or a current treatment team.

evidence.note: Lookup steps from general knowledge of Ontario crisis team practice; times estimated.

steps.name: Interview the patient and assess risk
steps.description: The crisis clinician interviews the patient in a private room: the events leading to the visit, mood and psychotic symptoms, substance use, suicide and violence risk factors and protective factors, supports and what the patient wants. A security officer stays nearby when risk is high.

error.defect_description: Risk misjudged because collateral is missing.

evidence.note: Interview of 30 to 90 minutes from general knowledge of crisis assessment practice.

steps.name: Gather collateral information
steps.description: With consent where possible (or without it when risk is serious), the clinician phones family, the family physician, the community mental health worker or group home staff to confirm the history, the safety of going home and who can support the patient.

control.basis: Personal Health Information Protection Act: consent or a permitted disclosure to reduce serious risk of harm

evidence.note: Collateral calls are standard crisis practice; times include unanswered calls and call-backs. Author's estimate.

steps.name: Document the assessment and recommend a disposition
steps.description: The clinician writes the crisis assessment note with a risk formulation and recommends either discharge with follow-up or psychiatric assessment, and discusses it with the emergency physician.

error.defect_description: Note missing key risk details used by the psychiatrist or follow-up clinic.

evidence.note: Share sent to psychiatry is the author's estimate for a community hospital crisis team.

steps.name: Agree the discharge (ED physician)
steps.description: The emergency physician reads the crisis note, reassesses the patient briefly and agrees to discharge; if the patient was on a Form 1 the physician ends the detention and documents why.

control.basis: Mental Health Act: only a physician can end a Form 1 detention; discharge on physician order

evidence.note: ED physician queue of 5 to 90 minutes between other patients; author's estimate.

steps.name: Call the on-call psychiatrist and present the case
steps.description: The crisis clinician pages the psychiatrist on call, presents the history, risk and collateral by phone and agrees when the psychiatrist will see the patient.

next.condition: psychiatrist on site or sees patient on morning rounds

evidence.note: On-call call-back times estimated.

steps.name: Drive in to see the patient after hours
steps.description: For urgent after-hours cases the on-call psychiatrist leaves home and drives to the hospital, usually 20 to 40 minutes away.

evidence.note: About one in five psychiatry consults are seen after hours by a psychiatrist who comes in; author's estimate.

steps.name: Assess the patient (psychiatrist)
steps.description: The psychiatrist reviews the crisis note, interviews the patient, decides on the diagnosis and risk, and chooses admission (voluntary or involuntary), discharge with follow-up, or transfer when no bed is available. Overnight non-urgent patients are seen on morning rounds.

control.basis: Psychiatric assessment by a physician before involuntary admission (Mental Health Act s.20)

next.condition: admit elsewhere: no bed in the corporation

evidence.note: At an academic hospital the 90th percentile time from physician assessment to an admission decision was 19.1 hours for mental health visits versus 10.9 for others (baia2019); the wait range and admission share are the author's estimate for a community hospital.

steps.name: Write admission orders and involuntary papers
steps.description: The psychiatrist writes the admission orders and, for an involuntary patient, completes Form 3 (Certificate of Involuntary Admission), gives the patient Form 30 notice and notifies the rights adviser; a Form 33 is added when the patient is found incapable of consenting to treatment.

error.defect_description: Form 3 or rights notice incomplete; detention open to challenge at the Consent and Capacity Board.

control.basis: Mental Health Act: Form 3 by a second physician, Form 30 notice and rights adviser

evidence.note: Form 3 must be signed by a different physician from the one who signed Form 1 after a separate assessment; Form 33 for incapacity (psychdb_f1). Forms 30 and the rights adviser notice are from the author's knowledge.

steps.name: Hand over to the ED for bed request and boarding
steps.description: The crisis clinician tells the ED charge nurse and the patient flow coordinator about the admission, enters the bed request on the bed board, and updates the patient and family on what happens next while the patient waits for a psychiatric bed.

evidence.note: Boarding in the ED until a psychiatric bed is ready is handled in ed-admission-boarding; at an academic hospital the 90th percentile ED stay for admitted mental health visits was 52.6 hours (baia2019).

steps.name: Arrange transfer to another hospital's psychiatric bed
steps.description: When the corporation's psychiatry unit is full, the patient flow coordinator phones other hospitals with psychiatric beds, sends the consult notes and forms by fax, and waits for an acceptance; the patient stays in the ED until then.

evidence.note: Out-of-hospital psychiatric bed searches can take hours to a day; author's estimate.

steps.name: Build a safety plan with the patient
steps.description: The crisis clinician works through a written safety plan with the patient and family: warning signs, coping steps, people and crisis lines to call, removing means such as medications, and when to return.

evidence.note: Safety planning practice from general knowledge of crisis services.

steps.name: Send the follow-up referral
steps.description: The clinician completes the referral to the hospital's outpatient mental health clinic, a rapid-access addiction clinic or a community agency, faxes it with the crisis note, and books or requests a follow-up appointment.

error.defect_description: Referral incomplete or sent to the wrong agency; follow-up missed.

evidence.note: Fax referrals were the norm in 2019-2022; author's knowledge.

steps.name: Discharge the patient from the ED
steps.description: The nurse gives the discharge instructions and safety plan, returns belongings from the security locker, confirms a safe ride home and closes the visit on the tracking board.

evidence.note: ED discharge tasks from general knowledge; times estimated.

steps.name: Report a patient who left before assessment
steps.description: If a patient leaves before the crisis assessment, the charge nurse informs the physician, phones the police with a description when the patient is on a Form 1 or at high risk, calls the family where appropriate, and files an incident report.

control.basis: Missing patient / elopement policy; Mental Health Act return of a person under Form 1

evidence.note: Elopement response from general knowledge of Ontario ED policies; share of about 4% estimated.

steps.name: Respond to a Code White
steps.description: When the patient becomes violent, staff call a Code White; four security officers and the nurse de-escalate, and if needed hold the patient while the physician orders restraint or emergency medication. The event is documented and reported as an incident.

control.basis: Code White procedure and least-restraint policy (Patient Restraints Minimization Act, 2001)

evidence.note: Code White team size and duration from general knowledge of Ontario hospital emergency codes; share estimated.

exceptions.name: Overnight arrival
exceptions.description: A patient cleared after midnight waits until the crisis team starts in the morning, under constant observation if held on a Form 1.

exceptions.name: Involuntary admission
exceptions.description: The psychiatrist certifies the patient on Form 3 and the patient boards in the ED waiting for a psychiatric bed.

exceptions.name: No psychiatric bed in the corporation
exceptions.description: The patient flow coordinator searches other hospitals for a bed while the patient waits in the ED.

exceptions.name: Patient leaves before assessment
exceptions.description: The patient walks out; police are called if the patient was on a Form 1.

exceptions.name: Violence during assessment
exceptions.description: A Code White interrupts the assessment.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from crisis consult request to ED discharge, admission order or transfer request

evidence.note: Derived by the author: at an academic Toronto hospital the 90th percentile total ED stay was 11.4 hours for discharged and 52.6 hours for admitted mental health visits, and the 90th percentile time from physician assessment to admission decision 19.1 hours (baia2019). This process starts after medical clearance and ends at the decision, before boarding.

benchmarks.population: Toronto Western Hospital mental health ED visits, 2012-2017

evidence.note: 29.3 hours for other admitted visits.

benchmarks.population: Toronto Western Hospital mental health ED visits, 2012-2017

evidence.note: 7.3 hours for other discharged visits.
Provincial ED length-of-stay target for admitted patients.

benchmarks.unit: minutes average after a joint protocol (125 before)

evidence.note: One hospital and one police force.

pain_points.description: Patients cleared overnight wait until the crisis team arrives in the morning, and psychiatrists see non-urgent patients on morning rounds, so the ED stretcher and a security officer are tied up for hours.

evidence.note: Mental health visits have much longer ED stays and decision times than other visits (baia2019); overnight coverage pattern from the author's knowledge.

pain_points.description: Constant observation of Form 1 patients by security officers or sitters is a large hidden labour cost.

evidence.note: Author's knowledge of Ontario ED staffing.

pain_points.description: Police officers wait in the ED until custody can be handed over.

evidence.note: Average waits of 80 to 125 minutes at one hospital.

pain_points.description: Paper Mental Health Act forms are error-prone; a defective Form 1 or Form 3 can make a detention unlawful.

evidence.note: Form requirements; error rates are not published.

pain_points.description: When the psychiatric unit is full, bed searches at other hospitals and boarding keep admitted patients in the ED for a day or more.

evidence.note: 90th percentile 52.6 hours for admitted mental health visits at an academic hospital.

sources.title: Analysis of emergency department length of stay for mental health visits: a case study of a Canadian academic hospital (D. T. Baia Medeiros, S. Hahn-Goldberg, E. O'Connor, D. M. Aleman), CJEM 21(3):374-383
sources.publisher: Cambridge University Press (Canadian Journal of Emergency Medicine)
sources.supports: Toronto Western Hospital, April 2012 to March 2017: 24,972 of 308,016 ED visits (8.1%) were mental health visits; 90th percentile ED length of stay 11.4 h for discharged mental health visits versus 7.3 h for others, and 52.6 h versus 29.3 h for admitted visits; 90th percentile time from physician assessment to admission decision 19.1 h versus 10.9 h.

sources.title: Improving hand offs between police and emergency departments (K. Born, A. Laupacis, M. Tierney)
sources.supports: A joint police-hospital protocol at St. Joseph's Healthcare Hamilton cut the average police wait in the ED from 125 to 80 minutes; under the Hamilton and Ottawa protocols hospital security takes over monitoring once a joint risk assessment or medical assessment allows the officer to leave; no provincial data on police wait times exist.

sources.title: Form 1, Mental Health Act: Application by Physician for Psychiatric Assessment (6427-41)
sources.publisher: Government of Ontario, Ministry of Health
sources.supports: A physician may sign Form 1 only after personally examining the person within the past seven days; it authorizes apprehension for 7 days and detention in a psychiatric facility for a maximum of 72 hours; the physician completes Box A (serious harm test) or Box B (incapable patient with a recurring disorder).

sources.title: Form 1 and Form 42 (Ontario Mental Health Act teaching page)
sources.supports: In an ED of a Schedule 1 facility the physician issues Form 1 and Form 42 at the same time and Form 42 must be given to the patient immediately; a Form 3 involuntary admission must be signed by a different physician after a separate assessment; Form 33 when the patient is found incapable.

sources.title: Time Spent in Emergency Departments
sources.supports: Provincial ED length-of-stay targets: 4 hours for low-urgency patients not admitted, 8 hours for high-urgency patients not admitted and 8 hours for admitted patients (the reported averages on the page are for 2025-2026, outside the reference period, and are not used).

assumptions: Describes the common practice of an Ontario community hospital ED crisis service in 2019-2022, not Halton Healthcare's own procedures.
Crisis clinicians work extended hours (roughly 08:00 to midnight), not overnight, as the organisation file's shift pattern says; overnight the ED physician holds high-risk patients until morning.
The process ends when the admission order is handed to ed-admission-boarding; the wait for a psychiatric bed is counted there, not here.

The organisation file's process map lists four roles; this workflow also uses ed_rn, ed_charge_nurse and bed_flow_coordinator, which exist in the organisation file. It also adds outputs to ed-discharge-home (ed_disposition), police (police_report) and qp-incident-management (incident_report), and the transfer request to ed-interfacility-transfer, which the map lacks.
Only the large-site ED resource (ed_spaces_otmh) is used; the same steps run at the two smaller sites.
Shares (Form 1 35%, police-brought 25%, constant observation 40%, psychiatry 55%, admission 38% of psychiatry patients, transfer 5%, elopement 4%, Code White 5%) are tier C estimates.

Simulated cycle time runs longer than the benchmark median because overnight waits for the crisis team and morning psychiatry rounds are included; the benchmark itself is a derivation from a downtown academic hospital with 24-hour psychiatry cover.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (wage times 1.35; physician figures are gross OHIP earnings).
